chmmc-cmm-2026-team-02.prompt: In acute scalene triangle $ABC$, the foot of the altitude from $A$ is $D$. $\ell$ is a line passing through $A$, and the feet of the altitudes from $B$ and $C$ to $\ell$ are $B'$ and $C'$, respectively. Show that the line through $B'$ perpendicular to $AC$ and the line through $C'$ perpendicular to $AB$ intersect on $AD$.
chmmc-cmm-2026-team-02.answer: Proof: coordinates with $A$ at the origin and $\ell$ the $x$-axis show both lines meet $AD$ at the same point

chmmc-cmm-2026-team-03.prompt: Justin and Eduardo play a game. There is a calculator with a display and two buttons: the first button replaces the number $x$ on the display with $\log_2x$ (unless $x\le0$, in which case it displays ERROR), and the second button replaces $x$ with $N^x$, where $N$ is a fixed positive integer greater than $2$. Justin chooses the value of $N$ and a positive integer to be initially displayed on the calculator screen. chmmc-cmm-2026-team-04.prompt: Let $S$ be a set of $2026$ points in 3D space placed by Ana, such that no three points in $S$ lie on a line. Ana chooses a starting point $P_0$ in $S$. Then Ana and Bob play a game on these points, with Bob moving first. (a) Bob chooses a point $P_1\in S$ distinct from $P_0$ and draws the segment $L_1=P_0P_1$. (b) Ana then chooses a point $P_2\in S$ distinct from $P_1$ and draws the segment $L_2=P_1P_2$, such that $|L_2|>|L_1|$. (c) The players continue to alternate: if the previous segment drawn was $L_k=P_{k-1}P_k$, the next player chooses a point $P_{k+1}\in S$ distinct from $P_k$ such that $|L_{k+1}|=|P_kP_{k+1}|>|L_k|$. (d) A player who cannot make a valid move loses. Over all sets $S$ of $2026$ points that Ana can choose, what is the maximum number of starting points $P_0\in S$ she can pick so that she will have a winning strategy?

chmmc-cmm-2026-team-05.prompt: Find all functions $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfying $f(n+1)^2-f(n)^2=2f(f(n))+1$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$. Here $\mathbb N$ denotes the set of positive integers.
chmmc-cmm-2026-team-05.answer: $f(n)=cn+\dfrac{c^2-1}{2}$ for a fixed odd positive integer $c$

chmmc-cmm-2026-team-07.prompt: Let $p$ be a prime, and let $\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z=\{0,1,\dots,p-1\}$ be the set of residues modulo $p$. For any two $2026$-tuples $a=(a_1,\dots,a_{2026})$, $b=(b_1,\dots,b_{2026})\in(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^{2026}$, and an integer $1\le i\le2026$, set $g_i(a,b)\equiv a_i+b_i+\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}a_jb_{i-j}\pmod p$ and $g(a,b)=(g_1(a,b),\dots,g_{2026}(a,b))\in(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^{2026}$. Show that for any $p\ne2027$ there exists a function $f:(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)^{2026}\to\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$ such that for any $a,b$ we have $f(g(a,b))\equiv f(a)+f(b)+\sum_{i=1}^{2026}a_ib_{2027-i}\pmod p$.
chmmc-cmm-2026-team-07.answer: Proof: use the formal logarithm of $1+\sum a_iT^i$; its $T^n$-coefficient has $p$-integral coefficients when $p\nmid n$
